key_insight: SymAnt combines neural networks with adaptable symbolic priors to anticipate long sequences of human actions from brief observations. Its central idea is to pair learned predictions with structured reasoning.
problem_solved: Anticipating many future actions from limited observations is difficult for purely neural models, which can also be hard to interpret and adjust.
method: Introduce a neuro-symbolic approach that combines neural expressiveness with symbolic structure.
Use adaptable symbolic priors to ground long-horizon action anticipation.
Note: The supplied abstract is truncated, so specific mechanisms and experimental results are unavailable.
impact: This approach could help practitioners build more interpretable and adjustable action-anticipation systems for human–robot interaction. Its empirical benefits cannot be assessed from the provided excerpt.

paper_title: SymAnt: Grounding Long-Horizon Action Anticipation with Adaptable Symbolic Priors
paper_authors: Fnu Aryan, Yaqi Xie, Joseph Campbell, Woojun Kim, Kwonjoon Lee
